decision.summary: The Fed cut its policy rate by 50 basis points, to 4.75%. The vote was 10-0.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate 50 basis points to 4-3/4 percent.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Economic growth was moderate during the first half of the year, but the tightening of credit conditions has the potential to intensify the housing correction and to restrain economic growth more generally.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Today’s action is intended to help forestall some of the adverse effects on the broader economy that might otherwise arise from the disruptions in financial markets and to promote moderate growth over time.

changes.quote: Readings on core inflation have improved modestly this year.

changes.quote: However, the Committee judges that some inflation risks remain, and it will continue to monitor inflation developments carefully.

tone_quotes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate 50 basis points to 4-3/4 percent.
The Committee will continue to assess the effects of these and other developments on economic prospects and will act as needed to foster price stability and sustainable economic growth.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 13.46% APR, a 50 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $2.08.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.5% and moved +2 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.46% would rise by about $3.94 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $30.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 4.6%, and employers added an average of 7k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.9% over the past year (August 2007); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -8 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.18% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 27%, cut 73%, hike 0%.
